title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'structures' (quasi-set-theoretic structures). The underlying data appear to be a set M of 'pieces' with a symmetric disjointness relation X || Y. For A ⊂ M, cosupp A = {Y ∈ M : Y || X for all X ∈ A} (the orthogonal A^⊥), and supp A = cosupp cosupp A (the biorthogonal closure). ΣM is the complete lattice of closed sets A = supp A, with orthocomplement C = cosupp. Page 79 asks whether infima in ΣM are 'computed by intersection' under a realization |·|: M → P(P). Under the strong neighbourhood hypothesis (every point is the support of some element), he proves that ⋀ corresponds to ∩. This page finishes that argument: from |X| ⊂ |A_i| one gets X ∈ supp A_i = A_i, hence X ∈ ∩A_i and x ∈ |∩A_i|.

He then states a Proposition. Let |·|: M → P(P) satisfy:
- Supp1: X || Y ⇔ |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅.
- Supp2: every x ∈ P is |X| for some X, i.e. {x} = |X|.

Extend |·| to subsets by |A| = ∪_{X∈A} |X|. Then:
- (i) |supp A| = |A| and |cosupp A| = P \ |A|.
- (ii) 1°) supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ |A| ⊂ |B| (equivalently A ⊂ supp B); 2°) A || B ⇔ |A| ∩ |B| = ∅.
- (iii) A ↦ |A| is an isomorphism of ordered sets ΣM ≅ P(P), compatible with the complement operations C.

In modern terms: an orthogonality space (M, ⊥) admitting a 'disjointness-faithful' set realization that hits all singletons has a Boolean, complete atomic lattice of orthoclosed subsets, canonically the power set of P. The marginal note says that without Supp2 one still gets a monomorphism (injection). Page 81 adds that P and |·| are then determined up to canonical isomorphism. It also tests the framework on topological examples (compact contractible 'liens', 'ficelles') where Supp2 fails.

Proof check:
- |cosupp A| ⊂ P\|A| follows from Supp1. For the converse, given x ∉ |A|, Supp2 gives X with |X| = {x}, and X ∈ cosupp A.
- Applying the cosupp formula twice gives |supp A| = |A|.
- 1°): X ∈ supp B ⇔ X || cosupp B ⇔ |X| ∩ (P\|B|) = ∅ ⇔ |X| ⊂ |B|.
- Surjectivity in (iii): take A = {X : |X| a singleton in S}.
- Without Supp2, |A| ⊂ |B| still implies supp A ⊂ supp B, so A ↦ |A| stays injective on ΣM but is no longer an order iso. This is consistent with the margin note.
errors: Item (i) as written/transcribed, '|A| = supp A', compares a subset of P with a subset of M. The intended statement is |supp A| = |A|; the line '|cosupp A| = P \ |A|' belongs to (i), the '(ii) Pour' being crossed out.
Implicit assumption: Supp1 forces X || X exactly when |X| = ∅. So the relation must be irreflexive except on 'empty' elements; this is not stated.
Minor: 1°) asserts an equivalence, but its 'i.e. A ⊂ supp B' only matches supp A ⊂ supp B because supp is a closure operator. Fine, but implicit.

missed.claim: The page is a step in Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 attempt to found 'analysis situs' (tame topology) on abstract 'structures' given by a disjointness relation. Points are recovered as a power-set realization of the lattice of supports, and the realization is unique up to canonical isomorphism (p. 81). This combinatorial-orthogonality approach to tame topology is not documented in the literature on Grothendieck's tame topology program.
missed.quote: L'application ΣM → P(P), A ↦ |A| est une iso. d'ensembles ordonnés correspondant aux op. C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest: it shows the Esquisse 'topologie modérée' idea being pursued via orthogonality spaces / point-free methods, a link to quantum-logic orthospaces and mereotopology not made in the literature. The mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine Galois-connection / orthogonality-space lemma, correctly proved. The only notable aspect is its role in the unpublished 1986 Analysis situs framework.
transcription_corrections: (i) should read '|A| = |supp A|' (or the intended '|supp A| = |A|'), followed by '|cosupp A| = P \ |A|' as part of (i); the '(ii) Pour' before it is struck out.
Condition labels are written as abbreviations of 'Supp' (S-upp^1, S-upp^2), with the first one initially started as 'Sim...' and struck.
Margin note: 'Ceci est valable sans Supp² et [donne] mais [seulement un] monomorphisme', with the arrow pointing to (iii).
